transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been struggling with constant, uncontrollable worry about almost everything in my life, including my work, family, and finances. This has been going on for over two years now, and I just can't seem to stop it.
Along with this constant worry, have you been experiencing physical symptoms like muscle tension, restlessness, feeling easily fatigued, or trouble sleeping?
I haven't really noticed those kinds of physical symptoms, like muscle tension or trouble sleeping. It's more that my mind just won't stop racing with constant, overwhelming worries all day long.
Do these persistent worries feel like intrusive, unwanted thoughts or images that pop into your head, and do you feel driven to perform certain actions or mental routines to make them go away?

Yes, they definitely pop into my head out of nowhere and make it really hard to focus on my daily tasks. I don't perform any specific actions or routines to make them go away, though—I just find it incredibly difficult to control or stop the thoughts once they start.
Over these past two years, have you also been feeling consistently down, depressed, or hopeless, or have you lost interest in activities you normally enjoy?
No, I wouldn't say I've felt depressed or lost interest in the things I enjoy. It's really just that I feel constantly overwhelmed and consumed by this non-stop worry and anxiety.
Have you noticed yourself feeling more irritable or easily annoyed than usual, or does your mind ever seem to go blank because of this constant worry?
I haven't really noticed feeling particularly irritable or having my mind go blank. Rather, I am just constantly consumed by the non-stop worrying and endless "what-if" thoughts.
How has this constant worrying affected your ability to function in your daily life, such as at work or in your relationships?

It has a huge impact on my ability to function, especially at work because these worried thoughts suddenly intrude and make it very difficult to focus on my tasks. I'm not really sure how it has affected my relationships, but the inability to concentrate on my daily work is a major struggle for me.
Have you struggled with focus, organization, or forgetfulness since your childhood, or did these concentration difficulties only start after you began worrying so much?

These concentration difficulties only started after I began worrying so much, about two years and three months ago. I never had any issues with focus or organization during my childhood. Now, my constant worries constantly intrude into my mind, making it very hard to pay attention to other tasks.

When these thoughts pop into your head, are they worries about everyday life things like work and family, or do they involve specific themes like contamination, hurting others, or needing things to be perfectly symmetrical?

They are definitely about everyday life things like my work, family, and finances. I don't have worries about contamination, hurting anyone, or needing things to be symmetrical. It is just constant, overwhelming anxiety about normal daily life.
Did this constant worrying start in response to a specific, major life event or stressor, or did it seem to develop gradually on its own?
I'm not really sure of any specific event that triggered it. It feels like it just gradually became a constant part of my life over the last couple of years.
